language.title: John Coll, edited by David Allen, BBC Microcomputer System User Guide
language.note: Acorn edition, part 0433 000, Issue 1 October 1984: procedures/functions, LOCAL, numeric types and assembly language. https://www.retro-kit.co.uk/user/custom/Acorn/8bit/BBCMicro/manuals/BBCMicroUserGuide.pdf

authorship.title: Computer History Museum, Sophie Wilson oral history
authorship.note: Interview by Douglas Fairbairn, 31 January 2012; retrospective account of BASIC and Acorn development. https://archive.computerhistory.org/resources/access/text/2012/06/102746190-05-01-acc.pdf

language.title: Apple Computer, Applesoft II Reference Manual
language.note: August 1978, Apple part A2L0006X: extended-precision floating-point language, graphics commands, cassette/ROM distinctions and memory controls. Original title pages credit Apple 1978 and Microsoft 1977.

language.title: Apple Computer, Apple II Reference Manual
language.note: Original machine documentation: Integer BASIC, memory and system interfaces; distinguish model/ROM configuration from language syntax.

spectrum.title: HiSoft, HiSoft BASIC manual, first edition
spectrum.note: October 1986; written by Cameron Hayne, preserved and corrected by the author. Compilation, OPEN#/CLOSE# directives, unsupported features and 128K differences. http://hayne.net/Spectrum/HiSoftBASIC/manual.html

editions.title: Centre for Computing History, HiSoft BASIC manual, CH75962
editions.note: Held 1988 Amiga manual described as a fast interactive BASIC compiler. Catalogue description establishes a separate platform edition, not measured performance or universal source compatibility. https://www.computinghistory.org.uk/det/75962/HiSoft-BASIC/

workflow.title: HiSoft, ZX Spectrum Programmer’s Manual: Devpac
workflow.note: 1985 copyright. Read the identified transcription by Nele Abels-Ludwig (1998), converted by Robert J. Baker (1999): GENS3 editor/two-pass assembly and MONS3 registers/breakpoints. https://worldofspectrum.org/pub/sinclair/games-info/h/HiSoftDevpacV3.pdf

platforms.title: HiSoft, Amiga Devpac manual, German edition
platforms.note: Translator’s introduction and GenAm/MonAm descriptions distinguish the Amiga package from Spectrum GENS/MONS. https://www.retrozone.ch/docs/amiga/HiSoftDevpac.pdf

altair.title: MITS, Altair BASIC Reference Manual
altair.note: 1975 original: numbered programs, direct mode, 4K/8K/Extended distinctions, loading, memory and conversion notes. https://altairclone.com/downloads/manuals/BASIC%20Manual%2075.pdf

adaptations.title: Apple Computer, Applesoft II Reference Manual
adaptations.note: August 1978 title pages credit Microsoft 1977; machine-specific graphics and memory statements.

adaptations.title: Sony, MSX-BASIC Programming Reference Manual
adaptations.note: Original PLAY and graphics command documentation establishes platform extensions, rather than universal Microsoft BASIC syntax.

notation.title: Sony, MSX-BASIC Programming Reference Manual
notation.note: Music PLAY reference: note letters, octave, length, tempo, strings and up to three simultaneous parts. MSX dialect only. Original manufacturer manual.

practice.title: Yuzo Koshiro, Kikizo interview, 14 October 2005
practice.note: Participant explains PC-88 development and his heavily modified MML-derived Music Love system. Retrospective testimony; not a universal MML grammar or chip specification.

design.title: Niklaus Wirth, The Programming Language Pascal, Revised Report
design.note: ETH Zurich, July 1973, sections 1–2 visually checked: teaching and implementation aims; declarations, scalar types, arrays, records, sets and files. https://www.standardpascaline.org/The_Programming_Language_Pascal_1973.pdf

context.title: Kyan Software, Pascal advertisement
context.note: 1986 contemporary advertising cited in BASIC Curricula: evidence of commercial/education positioning, not independent proof of speed claims.

implementation.title: K. V. Nori, U. Ammann, K. Jensen and H. H. Nägeli, The PASCAL P Compiler: Implementation Notes
implementation.note: ETH report 10, December 1974, abstract: compiler for a Pascal subset, targeting a hypothetical stack computer. https://www.standardpascaline.org/The_Pascal_P_Compiler_implementation_notes.pdf

squeak.title: Dan Ingalls, Ted Kaehler, John Maloney, Scott Wallace and Alan Kay, Back to the Future: The Story of Squeak, a Practical Smalltalk Written in Itself
squeak.note: OOPSLA 1997, pp. 318–326; VPRI TR-1997-001. Original authors describe Smalltalk-80 implementation, image, VM, Smalltalk-to-C translation, portability, graphics and sound. https://smalltalkzoo.computerhistory.org/papers/Back%20to%20the%20Future.PDF

scratch.title: Scratch Foundation, Scratch 1.4 source distribution
scratch.note: Original project source and documentation establish Squeak implementation of Scratch 1.4; not a claim about every later Scratch version. https://github.com/scratchfoundation/Scratch_1.4

book.title: Atari, De Re Atari, APX-90008
book.note: Original APX-distributed copy: cover, contents, preface credits, display-list, sound and GTIA sections. Cover is dated MCMLXXXI and signed L. Cross ’81; this is not used to assign a release date to every edition. https://www.atariarchives.org/dere/

book.title: Duncan Smeed and Ian Sommerville, Inside the Dragon

Consulted dv8 remaster (2017), fifth revision January 2021: title/copyright pages, contents, CRTC chapter 18 and VIA chapter 22. Remaster identifies itself at https://stardot.org.uk/forums/viewtopic.php?f=42&t=17242

comparison.title: John Coll, edited by David Allen, BBC Microcomputer System User Guide
